# 0007. Static HTML reports from snapshots, generated by a command

## Context and problem statement

[ADR 0004](0004-local-csv-snapshots-outside-the-app.md) keeps dated **Snapshots** as CSV files outside the app and
leaves "evolution reports over snapshots (per **Category**, per **Person**, over time), on this format, in a separate
piece of work" as a follow-up. Today the three snapshot commands (`snapshot record|link|check`) record, open and check
rows, but nothing shows how a **Person** grew. A manager can only open one **Share link** at a time or rebuild the
history by hand in a spreadsheet.

Managers want a report they can open, print or keep: plain HTML, with as little JavaScript as possible, made from the
**Snapshots folder** with one command. The question is where that report is generated, how it reuses the domain rules,
where it is written, and how it treats data that the **Ladder** has changed since it was recorded.

Two constraints frame the answer. The app does not open snapshots and does not compare several **Persons**
(`docs/PRODUCT.md`, non-goals). And a missing **Category** column means "not recorded", which is not **Level** 0
(ADR 0004), while `overallPercentage()` and `roleGap()` in `src/model.ts` treat a missing level as 0, so an old
**Snapshot** would seem to lose **Overall progress** as soon as a **Category** is added to the **Ladder**.

## Decision drivers

- **Security / privacy:** a report gathers more personal data than a single **Share link**. It must stay on the
  user's machine, never reach `dist/` or the dev server, make no network request when opened, and escape every value
  read from a CSV that may have been edited by hand.
- **Maintainability:** **Progress**, **Overall progress**, **Role gap** and the radar keep one implementation each
  (`src/model.ts`, `src/components/RadarChart.tsx`). The snapshot reading and validation stay in `scripts/snapshots.ts`
  and `scripts/csv.ts`.
- **Cost / simplicity:** no new dependency, no backend, no JavaScript in the report. It works the same in a fork and
  in an **Adopter repository** ([ADR 0005](0005-radar-as-a-dependency-of-an-adopter-repository.md)).
- **Robustness:** a **Ladder** change never makes history look wrong: "not recorded" is never counted as **Level** 0.

## Considered options

1. **A command that writes one self-contained static HTML file**, rendered with React on the server
   (`renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server`, already a dependency), reusing `model.ts` and `RadarChart.tsx`.
2. **A second Vite page** (`report.html`) that receives the snapshots through a virtual module at build time. Puts
   personal data in a bundle that can end up in `dist/` and be deployed, and needs JavaScript to render.
3. **The app opens the CSV files** (a file input). Contradicts ADR 0004 and the non-goal on several **Persons**.
4. **HTML written with string templates** in the command. Needs escaping by hand of names and tags from the CSV, and
   a second implementation of the radar.
5. **No report**: keep pointing to spreadsheets. Gives no evolution and no radar.

## Decision outcome

Chosen option: **"A command that writes one self-contained static HTML file"** (option 1), because it is the only one
that keeps personal data out of any bundle, escapes CSV content by construction, reuses the domain rules and the radar
as they are, and adds no dependency.

### The command

- `progression-radar snapshot report`, with the npm script `snapshot:report` in upstream and in the Adopter
  repository, next to the other snapshot scripts. It is loaded through Vite's `runnerImport` like them, so it gets the
  **Configuration** with `loadConfig()`.
- By default it reads the whole **Snapshots folder**. Arguments narrow it (a list of snapshot files, `--id` for one
  **Person**, a date range); filters are arguments, not JavaScript in the page.
- It reads snapshots with the code `snapshot:check` uses. Errors stop the report, as an invalid **Configuration** stops
  `build`. Warnings are printed and listed in the report.
- It prints only the path of the file it wrote and the problems found, never names or levels.

### What the report shows

- Every **Snapshot** is read with the current **Configuration**, as `check` and `link` do: the columns of unknown
  **Category keys** and unknown roles are listed as warnings, and levels above the **Highest level** are shown as
  recorded and flagged.
- Per **Person** (rows with the same **Person id**): a table of **Categories** by date with the **Reached level**,
  the **Overall progress** and the **Role gap** to the **Compared role** at each date, and one radar that overlays the
  first and the last date.
- For the team (the **Team overview**): a table of **Persons** by **Categories**, each **Person** at their latest row in
  any **Snapshot**, with the date of that row.
- The exact layout is not part of the public contract and can change in a minor or patch version.

### Not recorded is not Level 0

- **Overall progress** and the **Role gap** of a row are computed only over the **Categories** it recorded, and the
  report says how many it covers ("9 of 10 categories"). A "not recorded" cell is shown as such, never as 0.
- The rule lives in `src/model.ts`, as pure functions next to `overallPercentage()` and `roleGap()`, so the report does
  not have rules of its own. The app keeps its behaviour: a **Share link** holds every **Category**.

### The file

- One HTML file with its CSS inline and the radar as inline SVG, no `<script>`. Collapsible sections use `<details>`.
  It prints well, like the app.
- A `Content-Security-Policy` `<meta>` (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:`) so it makes no
  request even when opened from an e-mail. System fonts, or fonts embedded in the file; never a third-party request.
- Its CSS is a small stylesheet of its own that uses the same custom properties as `src/styles.css`, followed by the
  resolved `theme.css`, so it carries the adopter's branding.
- Written to `reports/` in the working directory (or the path in `--out`). Never inside the **Snapshots folder**,
  where `snapshot:check` warns about any file that is not `.csv`, and never inside `dist/`. A report is derived from
  the snapshots and can be written again, so the command replaces a report with the same name.
- `reports/` is git-ignored upstream, `init` adds it to the Adopter repository's `.gitignore`, and the dev server does
  not serve it: `server.fs.allow` does not cover it in an Adopter repository, and in a fork, where it is under Vite's
  root, the dev server answers 404 to any URL into it or into the **Snapshots folder**.

### The skill

- The `progression-radar-snapshots` skill drives `snapshot:report` like the other commands and relays the path and the
  problems. It does not read, summarise or interpret the report: that would be assessing a **Person**.

### Consequences

- **Good:** evolution per **Person** and a team view with one command, as a file that opens anywhere, offline and
  printable. One implementation of every rule and of the radar. No dependency, no JavaScript, no new place where the
  app reads personal data. History stays right after **Ladder** changes.
- **Trade-offs:**
  - `RadarChart.tsx` and the custom properties of `src/styles.css` gain a second consumer; changes to them must keep
    rendering on the server (no browser APIs in the chart).
  - A report is a copy of personal data in one more place, and people may send it around. The user owns that choice,
    as with the CSV files.
  - Reading old snapshots with the current **Configuration** means a renamed **Category key** shows as two
    **Categories**; the warnings say so, and fixing it is editing the CSV by hand.
  - The command and the npm script name join the public contract ([ADR 0005](0005-radar-as-a-dependency-of-an-adopter-repository.md)),
    which is a minor version.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - Add the "recorded categories only" functions to `src/model.ts` with their tests.
  - Implement the command in `scripts/`, its tests on temporary folders, and cover it in `scripts/adopter-fixture.mjs`.
  - Add `reports/` to `.gitignore`, to `init` and to the folders the dev server does not serve.
  - Update the skill, `docs/guides/snapshots.md`, `docs/PRODUCT.md` ("What it does"), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
    ("Layout", "Snapshots outside the browser"), `docs/UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md` (**Report**) and the README.
